title: First 100 Days - Reliability Orbit Onramp
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a time-boxed, cross-functional plan to get product teams and platform partners into an operational rhythm for SLO-driven reliability. The aim is to reach a repeatable 'orbit' where teams can define, measure, and iterate SLOs and guardrails with minimal SRE hand-holding by day 100.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: public-facing inference routes, background batch embedding jobs, and the Redwood Console telemetry pipeline for latency/cost signals.
- Not in scope: infra-only recovery automation (separate infra runbook).
- Assumes basic observability (traces/metrics/logs) exists for target services and teams have access to the Redwood Console and project-level dashboards.

High-level success criteria (end of 100 days):
- Each participating product team has an agreed SLO (1–2 signals) and defined error budget policy.
- Monitoring that emits SLO burn alerts and a lightweight runbook for first responders.
- Two cross-team canary rollouts using the rollout policy template demonstrating safe degradation fallback.
- Playbook artifacts committed to the shared reliability repo and linked from Confluence.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (eng-sre) — overall orchestration, stakeholder updates.
- Reliability coach per product: SRE on-call rotation volunteers (Marco H., Priya R.).
- Product owners: feature/product managers for each participating team (named in each sprint card).
- Observability owners: Platform Observability (Evan L.) — dashboards, SLO math verification.
- Console/rollouts: Console product manager (Ruth T.) — rollout tooling and canary configs.
- Exec sponsor: VP Platform Engineering (TBD).

Plan cadence and ceremonies:
- Weekly orbit standup (30 min): program lead + reliability coaches + product owners. Agenda: SLO status, blockers, upcoming canaries.
- Biweekly SLO design clinic (60 min): open office hours where SREs pair with product engineers on SLO definitions and queries.
- Monthly exec sync (30 min): highlight metrics and ask for resource decisions.
- Incident retro slot (ad hoc): any triggered SLO burn > 50% of budget requires a 1-week follow-up.

Phased 100-day timeline:
Phase 0: Pre-flight (days -7 to 0)
- Confirm participating teams and create onboarding checklist (owner: Aisha).
- Inventory baseline signals and dashboards (owner: Evan).
- Ticket templates created in Jira (SRE-2101, SRE-2102).

Phase 1: Establish SLO foundation (days 1–30)
Goals: define SLOs, implement measurement, create alerting baseline.
Key activities:
- Week 1: Kickoff workshop (owners: Aisha + product owners). Outcomes: candidate SLOs, customer-impact mapping.
- Week 2: SLO smoke tests — validate metric production and cardinality concerns (owner: Evan).
- Week 3: Draft runbooks and first-responder checklists (owner: reliability coaches).
- Week 4: Configure burn alerts and Slack bridges (#slo-burn-channel) + basic dashboard (owner: Platform Observability).
Deliverables:
- Per-team SLO one-pager (goal, metric, target, window, alert thresholds).
- Jira epic created with implementation subtasks.

Phase 2: Runbook hardening and small rollouts (days 31–60)
Goals: prove alerting, runbooks, and one canary rollout.
Key activities:
- Simulated SLO burn drills (tabletop) with stakeholders to exercise runbooks.
- Canary rollout 1: low-risk change behind rollout policy and monitor SLO impact for 48h (owner: Console PM + reliability coach).
- Observability follow-up: reduce noisy signal sources, tune queries to reduce false positives.
Deliverables:
- Runbook revisions based on tabletop outcomes.
- Canary postmortem and lessons learned doc.

Phase 3: Operationalize and scale (days 61–100)
Goals: hand over to product teams, codify templates, embed SLO in release process.
Key activities:
- Canary rollout 2 across a traffic-weighted slice; test fallback to compatible model variant.
- Automation: basic alert-to-ticket integration (Jira) and on-call escalation mappings.
- Knowledge transfer workshops and checklist handoff.
Deliverables:
- SLO templates in Confluence and reliability repo.
- Handoff signoff for each product team (signed by product owner + reliability coach).

Operational artifacts and templates to produce:
- SLO one-pager template (title, stakeholder, metric name, target, window, burn policy, rollback triggers).
- Runbook template (symptom, triage steps, mitigations, rollback, postmortem triggers).
- Canary checklist (preconditions, monitoring list, abort criteria, rollback steps).
- Postmortem checklist focusing on SLO impact and remediation timelines.

Measurement and KPIs:
- SLO coverage: percentage of participating product routes with an active SLO. Target: 80% by day 100.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for SLO burn alerts. Target: < 15 minutes.
- Number of canaries executed and number with no customer-visible impact. Target: >= 2, at least 1 with automatic fallback used.
- Reduction in noisy alerts over Phase 2. Target: 50% fewer false positives on SLO queries.

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy or high-cardinality metrics cause alert fatigue. Mitigation: sampling, aggregation windows, and one-week tuning sprint with Observability owners.
- Risk: product teams resist adding SLO work into tight release schedules. Mitigation: executive-level prioritization and a small staffed ‘SLO surge’ to accelerate initial setup.
- Risk: rollout tooling limits our ability to do traffic-sliced canaries. Mitigation: Console team to provide temporary feature-flag based traffic routing.

Decision checkpoints and escalation ladder:
- Day 30 checkpoint: SLOs defined for all onboarded teams (program lead signoff). If not met, schedule a focused 2-week remediation with exec sponsor involvement.
- Day 60 checkpoint: First canary complete and runbooks exercised. If not met, freeze new rollouts and extend Phase 2 by 2 weeks.
- Escalation ladder: Reliability coach -> Program lead -> Platform PM -> VP Platform Engineering.

Communication and docs:
- Primary doc hub: Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Orbit+Onramp+Main (owners must link artifacts).
- Weekly summary to #platform-ops Slack and monthly exec notes.
- All runbooks and SLO templates stored in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reliability-playbooks (PRs required).

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Confirm team list and upsert Jira epics SRE-2101..SRE-2105 (owner: Aisha).
2) Book SLO clinic slots and kickoff workshop invites (owner: Marco).
3) Observability owners to run a metric quality check and share findings (owner: Evan).
4) Console PM to prepare canary checklist draft (owner: Ruth).

Appendix: quick SLO examples (starter suggestions)
- Inference API: 95th percentile generation latency < 600ms over a 7d window; error budget policy: 0.5% p50 request failure rate per 30d, alert at 40% burn.
- Embedding pipeline: daily job completion within 3h for 99% of tenant batches; alert when > 10% of batches exceed window.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic — start small, prove, iterate. Feedback requested on the Day 1 workshop agenda and the acceptance criteria for a team handoff.

Document history:
- Drafted 2026-01-10 by Aisha Patel.
- Workshop outcomes and edits: 2026-01-21 (Marco), 2026-02-05 (Evan), 2026-02-28 (Ruth).
